citation.authors: de Jesus Gomes G, et al.
citation.title: Multiple Shorter High-Intensity Interval Exercise Sessions During the Day Result in Greater Energy Expenditure With Less Exertion Than a Longer Single Session: A Randomized Crossover Clinical Trial

reported.what: mean oxygen uptake during the 21 min of HIIE, 1xHIIE and 3xHIIE (2.86 and 2.81 L/min), with body mass 79.19 kg (Table 1): 36.1 and 35.5 mL/kg/min, level (36.12 - 3.7)/31.7 = 1.023 and about 1.00, at or above the activity scale's maximum of 1; the bout is entered by no other route (90% of the printed VO2max of 48.24 mL/kg/min would be 1.25)

heart rate during exercise, 1xHIIE and 3xHIIE (140 ± 12.3 and 139 ± 12.5 bpm), and blood lactate after the session (abstract: 7.7 ± 3.7 and 5.4 ± 1.8 mmol/L): all depend on the bout, which cannot be given

detail: The bout's mean level (1.02, from the measured 2.86 L/min over 79.19 kg) is now within the 0-2 activity scale, but the bout is 1 min work and 1 min recovery intervals whose work and recovery intensities are not printed (only the 21 min mean VO2), so a single level misstates the bout; the only clean printed outcome is the post-session blood lactate (7.7 +/- 3.7 mmol/L in the abstract), which is exactly what the interval pattern drives. The exercise heart rates (140 and 139 bpm in the Results, 158 and 147 bpm in the abstract) and the resting values (HR SD of 7.3 or 8.28 bpm; resting VO2 swapped between Table 3 and the text) are inconsistent within the paper, and the pre-exercise meal 2 h earlier is printed only as percentages (65% carbohydrate, 15% protein, 20% fat), so the fed state is unknown.
